titleEn: Messy, risky outdoor play is important for children, but adults can stop them enjoying it
titleZh: 脏乱且带点风险的户外游戏很重要，但成年人可能妨碍孩子享受它
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: There is growing evidence that children today have fewer opportunities for independent, adventurous outdoor play and fewer chances to make decisions and shape their own experiences than previous generations.
paragraphs.zh: 越来越多的证据表明，与前几代人相比，今天的儿童独立、冒险的户外游戏机会越来越少，做出决定和塑造自己经历的机会也越来越少。

paragraphs.en: Just 43% of children and young people aged from eight to 15 in England report spending time outdoors every day or most days. Research suggests that outdoor play has declined by 50% within a generation.
paragraphs.zh: 在英国，只有43%的8至15岁的儿童和青少年每天或大部分时间都在户外活动。研究表明，户外活动在一代人的时间内减少了50%。

paragraphs.en: Despite this decline, outdoor play is still often viewed as an opportunity for children to learn to manage risk and develop both their confidence and independence.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管这种下降，户外游戏仍然经常被视为一个机会，让孩子们学习管理风险和发展他们的信心和独立性。

paragraphs.en: My research explored how children make decisions when playing outside. The findings suggested that when young children hold back and resist risky play outdoors, it is rarely because they lack confidence or even access. Instead, they are responding to the subtle messages adults convey about risk, mess and safety.
paragraphs.zh: 我的研究探讨了孩子们在户外玩耍时是如何做出决定的。研究结果表明，当幼儿在户外阻止和抵制危险的玩耍时，很少是因为他们缺乏信心，甚至是缺乏机会。相反，他们是在回应成年人传达的关于风险、混乱和安全的微妙信息。

paragraphs.en: I carried out the research in a school, in collaboration with a nursery teacher. Our participants were children aged three to five who were enrolled in nursery and reception, meaning the school’s outdoor environment was familiar to them.
paragraphs.zh: 我与一位幼儿园老师合作，在一所学校进行了这项研究。我们的参与者是3到5岁的儿童，他们在幼儿园和接待处注册，这意味着他们对学校的户外环境很熟悉。

paragraphs.en: We combined observations of children’s play with small focus groups in which children took photographs to show what they liked and disliked about their outdoor environment. From these early conversations with the children, recurring patterns emerged. These children tended to avoid areas they associated with discomfort or danger, such as mud, water and climbing equipment, even though these spaces were familiar to them and adults were not restricting their access.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将对儿童游戏的观察与小组讨论相结合，在小组讨论中，儿童拍摄照片，以显示他们对户外环境的喜欢和不喜欢。从与儿童的早期对话中，出现了反复出现的模式。这些儿童倾向于避免与不适或危险相关的区域，如泥，水和攀爬设备，即使这些空间对他们来说是熟悉的，成年人也没有限制他们进入。

paragraphs.en: Children expressed things such as “I might fall”, “I don’t want to get wet”, and “My teacher doesn’t let me”. These were not spontaneous fears; they were reflections of the messages the children had repeatedly heard from adults.
paragraphs.zh: 孩子们表达了诸如“我可能会摔倒”、“我不想淋湿”、“我的老师不让我”之类的话，这些都不是自发的恐惧，而是孩子们反复从大人那里听到的信息的反映。

paragraphs.en: During our observations, we heard staff within the setting sometimes offering cautions such as “be careful”, “don’t climb too high”, and “watch out” during the children’s free play within the outdoors environment.
paragraphs.zh: 在我们的观察中，我们听到工作人员在设置有时提供警告，如“小心”，“不要爬得太高”，和“小心”，在孩子们的自由发挥在户外环境。

paragraphs.en: During our follow-up conversations with the children, they also described similar warnings from parents and carers. One child explained, “My mum doesn’t let me climb because I bumped my nose once”. These repeated messages had a lasting impact on how the children perceived risk. Over time, they absorbed these warnings and began to guide their own behaviour. Their hesitancy was learned, not innate.
paragraphs.zh: 在我们与孩子们的后续谈话中，他们也描述了来自父母和看护者的类似警告。一个孩子解释说，“我妈妈不让我爬，因为我撞到了鼻子”。这些重复的信息对孩子们如何看待风险产生了持久的影响。随着时间的推移，他们吸收了这些警告，并开始指导自己的行为。他们的犹豫是后天习得的，而不是天生的。

paragraphs.en: Based on the children’s feedback and our observations, the school made changes to the outdoor environment. Staff reorganised equipment in the outdoor area so children could reach and use it more easily, and they began talking about risk in a more supportive way.
paragraphs.zh: 根据孩子们的反馈和我们的观察，学校改变了户外环境。工作人员重新安排了户外区域的设备，以便孩子们更容易接触和使用，他们开始以更支持的方式谈论风险。

paragraphs.en: The school created a risk‑management plan and shared it with the children so they understood what was safe and what they could try for themselves. Adults also started pausing before stepping in and used language that signalled trust: “have a go and see how it feels first”, “I’m here if you need me”, or “what’s your plan for climbing that?” rather than “be careful” or “don’t go too high”.
paragraphs.zh: 学校制定了一个风险管理计划，并与孩子们分享，让他们了解什么是安全的，以及他们可以为自己尝试什么。成年人也开始在介入之前暂停，并使用表示信任的语言：“先试试看感觉如何”，“如果你需要我，我在这里”，或者“你爬那个的计划是什么？”而不是“小心”或“不要太高”。

paragraphs.en: They also added aprons to areas children had previously avoided because they didn’t want to get messy, helping them feel more comfortable exploring those spaces.
paragraphs.zh: 他们还在孩子们以前因为不想弄脏而避免的区域添加了围裙，帮助他们在探索这些空间时感到更舒适。

paragraphs.en: Within weeks, children began using areas they had avoided previously, taking more physical risks and engaging in richer sensory play. They were getting muddy, experimenting with water and exploring different textures and materials.
paragraphs.zh: 几周之内，孩子们开始使用他们以前避免的区域，冒更多的身体风险，参与更丰富的感官游戏。他们变得泥泞，尝试水，探索不同的质地和材料。

paragraphs.en: We saw children choosing what they wanted to do outdoors, including climbing frames and using the mud kitchen they had previously avoided. They became more assured and more willing to explore, with their play increasingly driven by their own interests rather than adult direction.
paragraphs.zh: 我们看到孩子们选择他们想在户外做的事情，包括攀爬架和使用他们以前避免使用的泥厨房。他们变得更加自信，更愿意探索，他们的玩耍越来越多地由自己的兴趣驱动，而不是成人的方向。

paragraphs.en: Letting children take risks
paragraphs.zh: 让孩子冒险

paragraphs.en: This matters because risk taking is not just about climbing higher or running faster. It is central to how children develop confidence and build problem-solving skills and a sense of who they are. When children never get the chance to test their ideas, push their bodies or make small mistakes, they miss out on experiences that build resilience and agency.
paragraphs.zh: 这一点很重要，因为冒险不仅仅是爬得更高或跑得更快。它对孩子们如何培养自信、建立解决问题的技能和自我意识至关重要。如果孩子们从来没有机会测试自己的想法、推动自己的身体或犯小错误，他们就错过了培养韧性和能动性的经历。

paragraphs.en: Many adults want children to be brave yet also want them to stay safe and clean. These two desires often collide. A child who hesitates at the top of a slide may not be lacking courage – they may simply be trying to avoid disappointing an adult who dislikes mess or worries about injuries.
paragraphs.zh: 许多成年人既希望孩子勇敢，又希望他们保持安全和干净。这两种愿望经常发生冲突。一个在滑梯顶部犹豫不决的孩子可能并不缺乏勇气--他们可能只是想避免让一个不喜欢混乱或担心受伤的成年人失望。

paragraphs.en: Supporting children’s risk taking doesn’t mean stepping back entirely. It means being intentional about the messages we send. Neither does supporting children’s ability to make decisions mean handing over unlimited choice to them. However, adults can support this by:
paragraphs.zh: 支持孩子们的冒险并不意味着完全退缩。这意味着我们要有意识地传递信息。支持孩子们做决定的能力也不意味着把无限的选择交给他们。然而，成年人可以通过以下方式支持这一点：

paragraphs.en: Reframing risk as learning, not danger.
paragraphs.zh: 将风险重新定义为学习，而不是危险。

paragraphs.en: Pausing before intervening, giving children time to assess situations themselves.
paragraphs.zh: 在干预之前先停下来，让孩子们有时间自己评估情况。

paragraphs.en: Allowing mess, recognising it as part of sensory and emotional development.
paragraphs.zh: 允许混乱，承认它是感官和情感发展的一部分。

paragraphs.en: Using language that signals trust, such as “I’m here if you need me” rather than “be careful”.
paragraphs.zh: 使用表示信任的语言，比如“如果你需要我，我就在这里”，而不是“小心”。

paragraphs.en: Offering meaningful choices, allowing children to make decisions and develop confidence in their own judgment.
paragraphs.zh: 提供有意义的选择，让孩子自己做决定，培养他们对自己判断的信心。

paragraphs.en: These small shifts help children feel capable rather than cautious. They also counter the growing cultural narrative that childhood should be clean, controlled and risk free.
paragraphs.zh: 这些小小的转变让孩子们觉得自己很有能力，而不是谨小慎微。它们也与越来越多的文化叙事相矛盾，即童年应该是干净的、可控的、没有风险的。
